evidence.claim: Russia’s president determines domestic and foreign-policy guidelines, serves as supreme commander, and is formally the guarantor of constitutional rights.
evidence.title: President of Russia: authority and responsibilities
evidence.excerpt: The supplied authority page establishes the constitutional role of the president.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official authority source, used only as context.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Formal presidential responsibility; not proof of personal orders.
contrary_evidence: Formal authority does not prove personal orders or operational control over every subordinate act.

evidence.claim: Article 80 of the Russian Constitution assigns the president responsibility for domestic and foreign-policy guidelines and makes the president the guarantor of rights and freedoms.
evidence.title: Constitution of the Russian Federation, Article 80
evidence.excerpt: Article 80 establishes the president’s formal responsibility for policy guidelines and constitutional rights.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Formal and direct constitutional attribution to the presidency.
contrary_evidence: Constitutional responsibility is formal and does not establish personal direction of each institutional act.

evidence.claim: In March 2022, Putin signed laws criminalizing reporting that deviated from official military information and discrediting the armed forces, with penalties of up to 15 years; independent outlets closed, relocated, or were blocked.
evidence.title: World Report 2023: Russia
evidence.excerpt: The 2022 legal changes criminalized nonofficial war reporting and discrediting the armed forces, while independent outlets were closed, relocated, or blocked.
evidence.canonical_fact_key: https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2023/country-chapters/russian-federation|2022 censorship laws|criminalization of nonofficial war reporting and discrediting
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Major rights-monitoring report with target-period coverage.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct attribution for Putin’s signature; implementation was institutional.
contrary_evidence: Independent reporting continued in reduced form and some alternative access remained.

evidence.claim: Russian authorities blocked major platforms and media, restricted VPNs, expanded biometric and facial-recognition surveillance, and adopted extrajudicial media-blocking powers.
evidence.title: Freedom on the Net 2022: Russia
evidence.excerpt: The 2022 internet environment included platform and media blocking, VPN restrictions, biometric and facial-recognition surveillance, and expanded blocking powers.
evidence.canonical_fact_key: https://freedomhouse.org/country/russia/freedom-net/2022|2022 platform and surveillance restrictions|blocking VPN biometrics facial recognition
evidence.ruler_attribution: State-institutional attribution; presidential responsibility is mediated.
contrary_evidence: VPN use and alternative platforms preserved some access.

evidence.claim: Roskomnadzor ordered media to use only official information about the invasion and threatened fines and blocking.
evidence.title: Russia: Media restrictions after invasion
evidence.excerpt: Roskomnadzor required use of official invasion information and threatened sanctions against noncompliant media.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Agency-level conduct; presidential responsibility is mediated.
contrary_evidence: Some independent outlets continued reporting before closure or relocation.

evidence.claim: Amnesty documented arrests, force, fines, searches, and outlet closures targeting journalists, monitors, and protest reporting; hundreds of journalists left Russia.
evidence.title: Russia: journalists and independent monitors being silenced
evidence.excerpt: Journalists and independent monitors faced arrests, force, fines, searches, and outlet closures in 2022.
evidence.canonical_fact_key: https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2022/11/russia-journalists-and-independent-monitors-being-silenced-to-stifle-reporting-of-protests-new-report/|2022 journalist repression|arrests force fines searches closures
evidence.ruler_attribution: State and agency conduct; personal attribution is limited.
contrary_evidence: Independent reporting and monitoring continued despite repression.

evidence.claim: After Putin’s September mobilization call, at least 1,386 peaceful protesters were detained, with reports of beatings and chokeholds.
evidence.title: Russia: more than 1,300 protesters detained
evidence.excerpt: At least 1,386 peaceful protesters were detained after the partial military draft announcement.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporary rights report with event-specific count.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Putin is directly linked to the mobilization call; specific police abuses are subordinate conduct.
contrary_evidence: The evidence documents protest and resistance as well as repression.

evidence.claim: Golos assessed 2022 regional and local competition as among the lowest in a decade, citing arbitrary candidate exclusion, politically motivated registration decisions, and intimidation through anti-extremism, foreign-agent, and army-discrediting laws.
evidence.title: 2022 regional and local elections
evidence.excerpt: Golos reported low competitiveness, candidate exclusion, politically motivated registration, and intimidation in 2022 elections.
evidence.canonical_fact_key: https://golosinfo.org/en/articles/146223|2022 regional and local elections|low competitiveness candidate exclusion intimidation
evidence.ruler_attribution: Electoral-system and administrative attribution; Putin responsibility is mediated.
contrary_evidence: Some smaller parties and candidates registered.

evidence.claim: Freedom House described Russia’s party system as managed, opposition competition as superficial, judicial independence as weak, and the 2020 constitutional amendments as enabling Putin to remain president until 2036.
evidence.title: Freedom in the World 2022: Russia
evidence.excerpt: The 2022 country assessment describes managed parties, superficial opposition competition, weak judicial independence, and constitutional entrenchment.
evidence.canonical_fact_key: https://freedomhouse.org/country/russia/freedom-world/2022|2022 managed party system|opposition judicial weakness constitutional entrenchment
evidence.ruler_attribution: Systemic and formal presidential attribution; not proof of every subordinate decision.
contrary_evidence: Formal institutions and some party competition remained.

evidence.claim: Russia held gubernatorial, regional-parliamentary, city-council, and municipal elections on 11 September 2022; official results showed pro-Kremlin candidates winning and Navalny-linked Smart Vote had no success.
evidence.title: Russia: regional (pseudo)elections in the shadow of war
evidence.excerpt: The September 11 elections included regional and municipal contests; pro-Kremlin candidates won and Smart Vote had no success.
evidence.canonical_fact_key: https://www.osw.waw.pl/en/publikacje/analyses/2022-09-15/russia-regional-pseudo-elections-shadow-war|lines 48-50|2022 regional elections results and Smart Vote failure
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Specialist regional analysis with precise lines.
evidence.ruler_attribution: System-level and mediated attribution through the governing political system.
contrary_evidence: Regional elections occurred and provided a formal avenue for participation.

evidence.claim: Incumbent or United Russia-backed governors won; United Russia and the mayor-backed My District movement won over 90% of Moscow municipal seats; Golos reported the lowest regional-parliament competitiveness indicator since 2012.
evidence.title: Russia: regional (pseudo)elections in the shadow of war
evidence.excerpt: Pro-Kremlin forces dominated gubernatorial and Moscow municipal outcomes, amid historically low competitiveness.
evidence.ruler_attribution: System-level and mediated through regional authorities.
contrary_evidence: Some opposition and independent activity remained.

evidence.claim: Independent campaigns were highly risky; candidates were excluded through politically motivated convictions or fake-news and army-discrediting cases; multi-day and online voting reduced observer scrutiny and enabled possible result correction.
evidence.title: Russia: regional (pseudo)elections in the shadow of war
evidence.excerpt: Candidate exclusion and reduced scrutiny constrained independent electoral activity.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Institutional and mediated attribution; no personal operational order established.
contrary_evidence: Some independent candidates still registered and campaigned.

evidence.claim: The Kremlin sought to display wartime consensus, marginalize elections in state media, and prevent unexpected outcomes; OSW characterized the elections as politically insignificant spectacles.
evidence.title: Russia: regional (pseudo)elections in the shadow of war
evidence.excerpt: OSW characterized the elections as a Kremlin-managed wartime consensus display with limited political significance.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Analytic Kremlin-level attribution; personal responsibility remains bounded.
contrary_evidence: The source is analytic and does not verify a personal order by Putin.

evidence.claim: CEC chair Ella Pamfilova said international observers were not provided for by the applicable legal framework; EPDE reported that Russian authorities used a restrictive interpretation excluding international observation.
evidence.title: No international politically-biased observers identified during the 2022 Russian regional elections
evidence.excerpt: The applicable framework was interpreted to exclude international observers from the 2022 regional elections.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Russian-authority and legal-system attribution; personal attribution is mediated.
contrary_evidence: Domestic electoral observation and formal election administration continued.

evidence.claim: The U.S. Department of State reported inability to change government through free and fair elections, restrictions on opposition candidates and campaign activity, limits on civil-society election monitoring, media suppression, and severe assembly and association restrictions.
evidence.title: 2022 Country Reports on Human Rights Practices: Russia
evidence.excerpt: The report records restrictions on elections, opposition, monitoring, media, assembly, and association in Russia.
evidence.canonical_fact_key: https://www.ecoi.net/en/document/2089062.html|lines 43 and 202|free and fair elections and restrictions
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Formal country human-rights report with explicit caveat on occupied areas.
evidence.ruler_attribution: National institutional outcome; presidential responsibility is systemic and mediated.
contrary_evidence: The report separately records abuses in occupied areas, which must not be generalized automatically to the Russian Federation.

evidence.claim: OVD-Info reported more than 21,000 detentions, at least 370 criminal-case subjects for anti-war speech or activity, more than 200,000 blocked internet resources, 19,478 anti-war detentions from 24 February, facial-recognition detentions in Moscow Metro, and repeated police violence.
evidence.title: Repressions in Russia in 2022
evidence.excerpt: The 2022 repression record included mass detentions, criminal cases, internet blocking, facial-recognition detentions, and police violence.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Specialist monitoring source with explicit denominator limitation.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct attribution to state enforcement; Putin attribution is direct for selected policies but mediated for individual incidents.
contrary_evidence: Counts are monitor-generated and are not complete national denominators.

evidence.claim: The 2022 record included environmental, labor-rights, anti-corruption, LGBT-related, Navalny-support, and anti-war actions; women comprised approximately 45% of identified anti-war detainees, rising to 51% and 71% in the 21 and 24 September mobilization protests.
evidence.title: Repressions in Russia in 2022
evidence.excerpt: Women formed a substantial share of identified anti-war detainees, especially during mobilization protests.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Monitoring data with explicit scope limitation.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Protest-policing and mobilization context; personal attribution is limited.
contrary_evidence: These figures measure identified detainees, not women’s overall political equality.

evidence.claim: A presidentially initiated Fundamentals of Russian Statehood curriculum promoted ideological unification, labeled dissenters as fifth column, foreign agents, or traitors, and framed the 2022 war narrative around Putinism and leader-sacrifice.
evidence.title: Scientific Putinism: Shaping Official Ideology in Russia
evidence.excerpt: The article links a presidentially initiated curriculum and 2022 war narrative to ideological unification and leader-centered Putinism.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Specialist analysis identifying a presidential initiative.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Stronger presidential attribution for the initiative; broader ideological effects remain interpretive.
contrary_evidence: The article is interpretive and does not prove a formal personality-cult decree.

evidence.claim: The September 2022 regional elections occurred amid wartime censorship; electronic and three-day voting reduced scrutiny, candidate-nomination rights were narrowed, and the unified system of public administration weakened democratic control of regional governance.
evidence.title: Russia’s regional elections 2022
evidence.excerpt: Wartime censorship, expanded electronic voting, narrowed nomination rights, and centralized regional administration constrained electoral control.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Academic-policy institute report with precise lines.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong institutional attribution; Putin responsibility is mediated through the presidential framework.
contrary_evidence: Regional elections still occurred and provided some formal avenue for participation.

evidence.claim: Ilya Yashin, Alexei Gorinov, and Yevgeny Roizman were arrested or prosecuted in connection with antiwar criticism; approximately 100 potential Moscow district candidates were excluded through administrative measures.
evidence.title: Russia’s regional elections 2022
evidence.excerpt: Antiwar opposition figures faced prosecution and approximately 100 potential Moscow candidates were administratively excluded.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Specialist policy analysis with precise lines.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct attribution is limited; national censorship framework attribution is stronger.
contrary_evidence: The source does not establish that Putin personally selected each target.

evidence.claim: Federal Law No. 60 restricted consultative election-commission members’ rights; regional commissions gained more control over campaign materials; and March 2022 legislation permitted more majoritarian electoral systems that benefited United Russia.
evidence.title: The 2022 elections as the last refuge of the scoundrel
evidence.excerpt: 2022 legislation changed election-commission rights, campaign-material control, and available electoral systems in ways favoring incumbent-party control.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Specialist monitoring analysis with linked legal materials.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Legislative and systemic attribution; formal presidential responsibility is coalition-mediated.
contrary_evidence: Not all eligible regions used the newly available majoritarian systems.

evidence.claim: At least 85 election-related persecution cases were identified; fake-news and military-discrediting laws were used against candidates; and a local electoral commission ignored alleged illegal campaigning by pro-Kremlin candidates while citing foreign-resource concerns.
evidence.title: The 2022 elections as the last refuge of the scoundrel
evidence.excerpt: Election-related persecution and selective enforcement constrained candidates while pro-Kremlin campaign conduct was reportedly treated more leniently.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Specialist monitoring source with precise locator.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong institutional and Kremlin-aligned electoral-administration attribution; personal attribution is mediated.
contrary_evidence: Some independent candidates registered and local activists continued voter mobilization.

evidence.claim: Six parliamentary parties could field candidates across all six legislative-election regions; some independent candidates registered; and local organizations urged opposition voting or invalid ballots.
evidence.title: The 2022 elections as the last refuge of the scoundrel
evidence.excerpt: Residual party, independent-candidate, and local mobilization activity persisted despite repression.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Specialist monitoring source, used as contrary context.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Not evidence of Putin liberalization; records residual political space.
contrary_evidence: The same source describes spoiler candidates, withdrawals, repression, and increasing risk for opposition activity.

evidence.claim: BTI reported that the president controlled parliament, no law could be adopted without prior Kremlin approval, courts were politically pressured, and the 2020 constitutional reform expanded presidential power and enabled continued rule potentially until 2036.
evidence.title: BTI 2022 Russia country report
evidence.excerpt: BTI describes executive dominance over parliament and courts and the operative expansion of presidential power.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Comparative governance assessment with precise PDF locator.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong formal and systemic attribution to Putin’s presidency; no proof of each individual decision.
contrary_evidence: Parliament and courts remained formally differentiated institutions and retained some routine functions.

evidence.claim: On June 11, 2022, Putin signed laws providing that post-15 March European Court of Human Rights judgments would not be implemented in Russia and would no longer ground reconsideration of Russian court decisions.
evidence.title: Putin signs laws on nonimplementation of ECHR judgments
evidence.excerpt: Putin signed laws rejecting implementation of post-15 March ECHR judgments in Russia.
evidence.source_locator: TASS HTML lines 72-90; Rossiyskaya Gazeta HTML lines 60-71
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Formal act reported by official sources and cross-checked.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct and high: presidentially signed legal act.
contrary_evidence: The laws retained limited compensation procedures for earlier judgments until January 2023 and created a domestic compensatory mechanism.

evidence.claim: Women faced no formal legal bar to participation but held approximately 15% of national legislative seats and only three of 31 cabinet positions; ethnic minorities participated but ethnic Russians dominated federal political and administrative institutions.
evidence.title: Russia 2022 Human Rights Report
evidence.excerpt: Formal participation was permitted, but women’s representation was low and ethnic Russians dominated federal institutions.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Formal human-rights report with precise PDF locator and stated limitations.
evidence.ruler_attribution: National institutional outcome; responsibility is mediated through presidential appointments and the governing system.
contrary_evidence: Women and minority citizens participated, and no explicit legal prohibition was identified.

evidence.claim: High incumbent support in ethnic republics was associated less with ethnic culture than with local administrations’ capacity to monitor and control rural voters; these mechanisms reinforced loyalty to federal political actors.
evidence.title: The Anatomy of Loyalty
evidence.excerpt: Local administrative monitoring and control mechanisms helped produce incumbent loyalty in ethnic republics.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Scholarly analysis; target-year specificity is partly contextual.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Weak-to-medium mediated attribution through regional administrations and federal structures.
contrary_evidence: The study rejects a simple ethnic-cultural explanation and does not establish uniform treatment across all republics.

evidence.claim: Putin signed the December 5, 2022 law extending LGBT propaganda restrictions to public, online, film, book, and advertising content involving people of all ages; rights groups described it as discriminatory and chilling expression, association, and participation.
evidence.title: Russia expands LGBT propaganda ban
evidence.publisher: Reuters republished by Euronews; Human Rights Watch corroboration
evidence.excerpt: Putin signed an expanded LGBT propaganda law covering public and private media and content involving all ages.
evidence.source_locator: Reuters HTML lines 642-669; HRW HTML lines 604-618
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters chronology corroborated by rights-organization legal analysis.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct presidential attribution for enactment; implementation was shared.
contrary_evidence: Russian authorities framed the law as protection of traditional values; full enforcement consequences within 2022 are not established.

evidence.claim: Carnegie described elite speculation and a virtual succession race but stated that Putin had not announced a departure, was not clearly preparing to leave office, and that the presidential administration was preparing for the 2024 election.
evidence.title: War in Ukraine Has Sparked a New Race to Succeed Putin
evidence.excerpt: The source reports succession speculation without a documented departure or transfer decision in 2022.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Specialist political analysis with precise locator.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Supports a no-event blocker only.
contrary_evidence: This is context about absence of a documented transfer event, not evidence of a transfer decision or negative ruler conduct.

evidence.claim: A commissioned VTsIOM telephone survey reported that 69% of respondents considered regional elections generally honest and 66% considered the results reliable.
evidence.title: Regional Elections 2022
evidence.excerpt: The survey reported majority perceptions of election honesty and result reliability.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Commissioned official polling with possible framing effects.
evidence.ruler_attribution: No direct ruler attribution; public-perception contrary evidence.
contrary_evidence: The poll was commissioned by a pro-government policy institute and may reflect question or framing effects; it conflicts with observer and monitoring evidence.

evidence.claim: Women and minorities had no formal legal bar to political participation, but women held approximately 15% of national legislative seats and three of 31 cabinet positions; ethnic Russians dominated federal political and administrative institutions.
evidence.title: 2022 Country Reports on Human Rights Practices: Russia
evidence.excerpt: Formal participation existed alongside low women’s representation and ethnic-Russian dominance of federal institutions.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Same report, independently mapped claim unit and precise locator.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Institutional outcome; presidential responsibility is mediated.
contrary_evidence: Women and minority citizens participated and no formal statutory prohibition was identified.

evidence.claim: National minorities actively participated in political life, but ethnic Russians, approximately 80% of the population, dominated federal political and administrative institutions.
evidence.title: 2022 Country Reports on Human Rights Practices: Russia
evidence.excerpt: Minority participation coexisted with ethnic-Russian dominance of federal institutions.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Institutional and outcome-based; systemic rather than personal attribution.
contrary_evidence: Minority citizens participated; the claim does not establish universal exclusion.

evidence.claim: State-aligned entities reportedly influenced employee voting; repression of civil society restricted election monitoring; and war-related restrictions effectively prevented traditional campaign events.
evidence.title: 2022 Country Reports on Human Rights Practices: Russia
evidence.excerpt: Employee voting influence, restricted monitoring, and limits on traditional campaign events were reported during the 2022 elections.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Formal country report with precise locator.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Institutional and mediated presidential responsibility.
contrary_evidence: Elections and formal campaigns still occurred.

evidence.claim: In September 2022, 20 women protesting the conscription of Chechens were detained and beaten by law-enforcement officers.
evidence.title: Human Rights Committee considers report on Russian Federation
evidence.excerpt: Twenty women protesting Chechen conscription were reportedly detained and beaten.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: UN meeting summary with event-specific locator.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct law-enforcement attribution; presidential responsibility is mediated through mobilization policy.
contrary_evidence: The event documents unequal exposure to repression, not women’s overall political representation.

evidence.claim: Migrants from the Caucasus and Central Asia, Muslims, Ukrainians, Roma, and refugees were reported targets of hate speech and violence; racial profiling and AI-supported targeting by law enforcement were also raised.
evidence.title: Human Rights Committee considers report on Russian Federation
evidence.excerpt: The review raised minority targeting, hate speech, violence, racial profiling, and AI-supported law-enforcement targeting.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: UN record with precise locator and contrary legal context.
evidence.ruler_attribution: State and law-enforcement responsibility; presidential attribution remains mediated.
contrary_evidence: Russian law formally protects against discrimination, though implementation was reported as inadequate.

evidence.claim: Institutionalized discrimination against LGBT persons and shrinking civic space for LGBT people and rights organizations were reported; the Duma was advancing broader restrictions in 2022.
evidence.title: Human Rights Committee considers report on Russian Federation
evidence.excerpt: The review reported discrimination and shrinking LGBT civic space amid advancing restrictions.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong state-policy attribution; Putin’s direct enactment is separately documented in E035.
contrary_evidence: The record concerns shrinking rights and civic space, not a complete prohibition on all LGBT political activity.

evidence.claim: In the 2022 regional elections, 9 of 29 eligible parties nominated no candidates; average party-list competition was the lowest since 2012, and self-nominated candidates declined compared with 2017.
evidence.title: Candidate admission in the 2022 regional elections
evidence.excerpt: Party participation and self-nomination declined, while average competition reached a low point since 2012.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Election-monitoring report with precise locators and countervailing candidate count.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Electoral-system and administrative outcome; Putin attribution is mediated.
contrary_evidence: 893 candidates were still nominated for regional parliamentary majoritarian seats and some contests remained formally competitive.

evidence.claim: The Russian CEC reported that more than 31,000 women were nominated in the 2022 unified voting day elections and approximately 16,000 women were elected across roughly 4,700 campaigns.
evidence.title: Women’s participation in 2022 elections
evidence.publisher: RIA Novosti reporting Russian CEC figures
evidence.excerpt: Official figures reported substantial numbers of women nominees and elected candidates in 2022.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official figures with aggregation and comparability limitations.
evidence.ruler_attribution: No direct ruler attribution; contrary contextual evidence.
contrary_evidence: The figures aggregate local, regional, and other offices and do not establish equal access to influential posts.

coverage.reason: Target-period evidence covers formal competition, regional elections, managed contestation, candidate access, and contrary public-perception material.
Evidence covers election competitiveness, candidate exclusion, monitoring restrictions, and residual participation.
Evidence covers opposition, protest, journalists, monitors, civic organizations, and repression, with mediated-attribution caveats.
Institutional weakness and a directly Putin-signed rejection of post-March ECHR judgments are documented; domestic institutional conduct is partly mediated.
Evidence covers executive dominance, leader-centered ideology, repression, and discriminatory policy; formal personality-cult evidence remains bounded.
Evidence covers censorship laws, official-only narratives, outlet closures, media blocking, and restrictions on expression.
Evidence materially covers women, minorities, LGBT persons, excluded candidates, ethnic republics, and protest repression, but regional representation data remain incomplete.
Institutional continuity and constitutional entrenchment are documented. No 2022 transfer or succession conduct was found; E036 is a context/blocker only.
Evidence covers platform and media blocking, VPN restrictions, surveillance, administrative harassment, and candidate/protest repression.
Target-period deterioration and wartime escalation are documented with inherited-condition, attribution, source-concentration, and contrary-evidence caveats.
